questions.q: What is the main advantage of dynamic routing over static routing?
options: It uses no CPU or bandwidth
Routers learn routes and adapt automatically when the network changes
questions.explain: Routing protocols let routers share information and update their tables when links fail or networks are added.
RIP counts the number of routers (hops) on the path.

questions.q: What is the maximum usable hop count in RIP?
questions.explain: A route with 16 hops is treated as unreachable, so 15 is the maximum usable hop count.

questions.q: Which type of routing protocol is OSPF?
questions.explain: OSPF is a link-state protocol. Each router builds a map of the area and runs the SPF algorithm.

questions.q: What do all OSPF routers in an area share?
questions.explain: Routers exchange LSAs until every router in the area has the same LSDB, and then each one calculates its own routes.

questions.q: What is OSPF's metric based on?
questions.explain: OSPF cost is calculated from the reference bandwidth divided by the interface bandwidth.

questions.q: A router learns the same network from both RIP (AD 120) and OSPF (AD 110). Which route is installed?
options: Both routes, one after the other
questions.explain: The route from the source with the lower administrative distance wins, so OSPF (110) beats RIP (120).

questions.q: What is the purpose of OSPF Hello packets?
options: To discover neighbours and keep adjacencies alive
questions.explain: Hello packets are sent regularly to find neighbours and confirm that they are still there.
